replication.target_description: Vacation positive-emotion response in anticipation versus retrospection. Supplied p. 40 Table 9a has separate Happiness, Mood, Enjoyment and Mean of DV1 tests; description does not specify which current-positive-emotion component or composite.

notes: Identity assessed from supplied canonical text: cover identifies Lau Tsz Chin, University of Hong Kong, 2020, title Van Boven and Ashworth (2007): Replication and extension, supervisor Dr. Gilad Feldman; provenance header names https://osf.io/ns26x and Cherry LAU Thesis Final Report.pdf. Page 3 gives the exact target original title and DOI 10.1037/0096-3445.136.2.289. This is a primary completed thesis report with methods, results and supplementary results, not a preregistration or secondary article. No PDF was supplied. Original side and unassigned fields are placeholders only. Target ambiguous: p. 15 distinguishes Hypothesis 7a current positive emotion from Hypothesis 7b predicted/remembered enjoyment. The supplied p. 40 contains four vacation DV1 comparisons: Happiness t = 1.57, p = .117, Cohen’s d = 0.13; Mood t = 2.14, p = .033, d = 0.18; Enjoyment of contemplation t = 1.17, p = .241, d = 0.10; Mean of DV1 t = 1.79, p = .074, d = 0.15. The neutral description does not identify a component or explicitly request the composite; no component selected by row order or numerical matching. A further candidate if intensity is intended as DV2 is p. 41 Vacation actual enjoyment t = -0.14, p = .890, d = -0.01. Common main-results condition N is a field-scope candidate only: Table 8a/8b 288 anticipation + 276 retrospection = 564 distinct participants; do not promote common N to a matched target while the outcome is unresolved. Main results follow general funneling but precede additional supplementary exclusions; supplementary p. 52 vacation groups are 243 + 241 = 484, with different tests on p. 58. Vacation was changed from skiing to a general resort vacation (p. 25).
